## How it works

- [statement] Hyperliquid's ADL fired during the Oct 10, 2025 cascade. The Defiant reports it 'forcibly closed profitable short positions'; CoinShares says Hyperliquid activated ADL on shorts while Lighter did not need to because its insurance reserves sufficed; CoinGecko calls it Hyperliquid's first cross-margin ADL in over two years; Chitra's v3 abstract says ADL was used repeatedly to close $2.1 billion of positions in 12 minutes. (high confidence) — https://thedefiant.io/newsletter/defi-daily/the-ultimate-10-10-crash-autopsy · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://coinshares.com/at/insights/knowledge/billions-in-liquidations-what-happened/, https://www.coingecko.com/learn/hyperliquid-hlp-vault-analysis, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01112v3
- [statement] The JELLY settlement drew centralization criticism because a validator vote, not autonomous contract logic, set the closing price. Arthur Hayes wrote 'Let's stop pretending Hyperliquid is decentralized' (Decrypt); Arkham said the manual closing price overrode autonomous contracts and showed a central point of control; OneKey said the intervention boundary was undefined beforehand; the community wiki records Bitget's CEO calling it 'FTX 2.0'. (medium confidence) — https://decrypt.co/311713 · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://info.arkm.com/research/jellyjelly-exploit-on-hyperliquid, https://onekey.so/blog/ecosystem/hyperliquid-incident-postmortem/, https://hyperliquid-co.gitbook.io/community-docs/introduction/roadmap/incident/2025-26-03
- [statement] Hyperliquid's on-chain fill log for 2025-10-10 records 34,983 ADL executions across 19,337 wallets and 162 tickers. CoinShares says Hyperliquid activated ADL on short positions while Lighter did not need to because its insurance reserves sufficed. CoinGecko calls it Hyperliquid's first cross-margin ADL in over two years. FTI warns that ADL closed some of the best-hedged shorts, which turns a hedged portfolio into a naked one. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v3 · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://coinshares.com/at/insights/knowledge/billions-in-liquidations-what-happened/, https://www.coingecko.com/learn/hyperliquid-hlp-vault-analysis, https://www.fticonsulting.com/insights/articles/crypto-crash-october-2025-leverage-met-liquidity

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Hyperliquid backstop liquidation: below 2/3 of maintenance margin the HLP liquidator vault can take over. A cross backstop transfers all cross positions and cross margin (the trader can end with zero equity); an isolated backstop transfers only that isolated position and margin. The maintenance margin is not returned to the user during a backstop, and backstop pnl goes to HLP depositors rather than the exchange operator. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison
- [statement] Hyperliquid's side of the ADL dispute: Jeff Yan said ADL 'does not transfer pnl to HLP', treats HLP symmetrically with users and 'has nothing to do with HLP or backstop liquidations', and that ADLs net made users hundreds of millions by closing profitable shorts at favorable prices. Dan Robinson argued the paper's model of Hyperliquid ADL was wrong because production ADL closes contracts rather than taking equity. A commentator notes Hyperliquid's ADL code is not open, so outsiders infer behavior from docs and fills. (medium confidence) — https://protos.com/outdated-algorithm-caused-650m-excess-losses-on-hyperliquid-report · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://thogiti.github.io/2025/12/11/Autodeleveraging-Hyperliquid-653M-debate.html
- [statement] Pattern across JELLY, POPCAT and Fartcoin: the attacker picks a thin-liquidity asset and engineers a liquidation so the backstop vault inherits the position. CoinGecko calls HLP's backstop role 'a predictable and repeatable target' while noting HLP's cumulative PnL never turned negative; OneKey notes HLP, unlike a market maker, cannot refuse positions once liquidation rules fire; Arkham called the vault the platform's central counterparty. (medium confidence) — https://www.coingecko.com/learn/hyperliquid-hlp-vault-analysis · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://onekey.so/blog/ecosystem/hyperliquid-incident-postmortem/, https://info.arkm.com/research/jellyjelly-exploit-on-hyperliquid

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Hyperliquid liquidation price formula (docs): liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side), where l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE, side = 1 for long and -1 for short, margin_available (cross) = account_value - maintenance_margin_required, and margin_available (isolated) = isolated_margin - maintenance_margin_required. For tiered assets, maintenance leverage comes from the margin tier matching position value at the liquidation price. The cross-margin liquidation price does not depend on the leverage setting; the isolated one does. Displayed estimates can drift with book liquidity, funding payments and unrealized PnL on other cross positions. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://docs.trade.xyz/risk-and-margining/liquidation-mechanics.md
- [statement] Scale of Hyperliquid ADL on Oct 10, 2025 per Chitra's v3 reconstruction (single origin): the on-chain fill log records 34,983 ADL executions across 19,337 distinct wallets and 162 tickers, with at least 40 recorded ADL events in one 10-minute period. Chitra says the same data show clustering of ADL events, which is why the paper models ADL as a multi-round game. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v3 · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison
- [statement] Hyperliquid's mark price takes external CEX prices as an input, so a squeeze on thin CEX or spot markets can move its liquidation prices. In the JELLY attack, CoinGecko, the community docs and Rekt report the price was pushed across Hyperliquid and other exchanges, which let the liquidated short reach HLP. (medium confidence) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://hyperliquid-co.gitbook.io/community-docs/introduction/roadmap/incident/2025-26-03, https://www.coingecko.com/learn/hyperliquid-hlp-vault-analysis, https://rekt.news/hyperliquidate2
- [statement] Hyperliquid liquidations can be audited from public artifacts, not source code. The node is closed source, so OtterSec reverse-engineered the hl-node binary. Historical blocks are available from s3://hl-mainnet-node-data/explorer_blocks. The public L2 order-book archive supports minute-level panels (Lim), the on-chain fill log supports per-fill ADL replay (Chitra), and the info API's vaultDetails endpoint returns HLP history (CoinGecko). Chitra notes Binance's account-level ADL data are not public. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://osec.io/blog/2026-06-22-hyperliquid-risk-engine · keywords: Hyperliquid and CEX liquidation comparison · also: https://journals.lincoln.ac.nz/index.php/JFDA/article/view/1395, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01112v3, https://www.coingecko.com/learn/hyperliquid-hlp-vault-analysis
